$comment: Documented differences between the five Content Security Policies compared by scripts/check-csp-parity.mjs (site and app-web from their vercel.json; desktop from tauri.conf.json; android from tauri.android.conf.json; ios from tauri.ios.conf.json). Each entry says in which policies a source is expected, and why it is absent from the others. A source present in every policy needs no entry. Keep the reasons honest: mark what is not verified.

exceptions.reason: Tauri's own schemes (tauri:, asset:, ipc:) exist only inside the app WebViews, desktop, Android and iOS. Those policies have no style-src or worker-src, so default-src carries what the web hosts put there: 'unsafe-inline' for styles and blob: for the bundled engine. Scripts have their own script-src (see the 'wasm-unsafe-eval' entry).

Tauri adds a hash of every bundled script and inline script to the desktop script-src when it serves a page, and a hash makes 'unsafe-inline' inert, so the desktop leaves it out. Inline scripts run because they are hashed, as on Alice Web, whose exported pages carry the same hashes in a meta policy.
The semantic engine compiles WebAssembly in Alice Web and its desktop, Android and iOS builds; 'wasm-unsafe-eval' allows that without allowing eval() or new Function(). The site runs no WebAssembly.
Cloudflare Web Analytics beacon, loaded by the public site only.
The desktop policy has no style-src: styles fall back to default-src, which allows 'self' and 'unsafe-inline'.
The desktop policy has no font-src: fonts fall back to default-src, which allows 'self'.

Alice Web embeds icon fonts as data URIs; the site serves its fonts from files. Not verified: the desktop bundles Alice Web but its default-src has no data:, so a data: font in the desktop build would be reported. Check with the crawl script before enforcing.
Tauri's asset protocol, in the desktop, Android and iOS apps only.
QR codes and generated images are drawn from blobs in the apps; the site shows no generated image.

Learn pack illustrations come from the packs repository (raw.githubusercontent.com) and its jsDelivr mirror; Alice Web and its desktop, Android and iOS builds share them. The site loads no remote image.
Tauri IPC between the page and the Rust side, in the desktop, Android and iOS apps.
On Android, Tauri's WebView reaches the Rust side through http://ipc.localhost instead of the ipc: scheme.
The site posts its analytics beacon to Cloudflare and calls the Worker by its exact host; the apps allow https://*.alicebtc.com instead.

Alice Web and the apps allow any HTTPS or secure WebSocket destination because Custom AI servers and custom Explorer nodes are chosen by the user and can be anywhere (a VPS, an Umbrel, an OpenAI-compatible API); a policy is the same for every user and cannot name the one server a user typed. Connecting to one's own node is a privacy gain. It does not prevent exfiltration by code that already runs (docs/security/web-storage-hardening.md, docs/security/csp-tools.md).

Plain HTTP and WebSocket stay allowed in Alice Web and the desktop for a Custom AI server or an Explorer node on the local network. The Android app leaves them out: Android refuses cleartext traffic in a release build, so a server there has to answer over HTTPS. The iOS app leaves them out too; whether App Transport Security would block cleartext without them is not verified.

The semantic engine runs in workers built from blobs. The site has no worker. The desktop has no worker-src: workers fall back to its script-src, which does not allow blob:. Not verified whether the desktop build starts a blob: worker; check with the crawl script on the desktop before adding one.
Learn embeds videos through the privacy-enhanced YouTube player, in Alice Web and its desktop, Android and iOS builds; the site embeds nothing.
A Tauri WebView cannot be framed by a web page, so the desktop policy leaves this navigation directive out. It has no default-src fallback.
The desktop bundle sets no base element and navigates only its own files; the directive has no default-src fallback.
Alice Web's enforced policy forbids any base element, a stricter value than the site's report-only 'self'. The desktop leaves the directive out (see the 'self' entry).
The desktop bundle submits no HTML form to a remote host; the directive has no default-src fallback.
The desktop policy has no object-src: plugins fall back to default-src. No plugin is loaded on any surface.
